claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service conditions.
The improved plastic strain and toughness arise from a pronounced disordered-solid-solution effect.
Chemical disorder in WTaTiVZr generates local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions reduce dislocation activation barriers.
Reduced dislocation activation barriers promote activation of additional slip systems.
Activation of additional slip systems enables more uniform plastic deformation and delays brittle fracture.
The initial WTaTiVZr material is a single-phase, likely BCC, equimolar solid solution.
WTaTiVZr has significant local lattice distortion compared with the homogeneous lattice of pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr contains compositional heterogeneity that modifies dislocation core structures.
Local stress fields produced by intrinsic chemical disorder lower the Peierls barrier for dislocation motion in WTaTiVZr.
Lowering the Peierls barrier facilitates cross-slip and enhances plastic accommodation.
Pure tungsten is more prone to brittle behavior because it has higher dislocation activation barriers.
The proposed mechanism applies while WTaTiVZr remains a single-phase homogeneous BCC material without significant precipitation or phase segregation.
Secondary-phase formation or extreme irradiation may invalidate the proposed mechanism by altering the relevant microstructure.
A controlled comparison should test WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten at 800–1200°C using equivalent geometry, thermal history, atmosphere, and loading conditions.
Plastic strain, fracture toughness, stress–strain response, dislocation structure, phase purity, and lattice parameters can be measured to test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain more than 20% improvement in both plastic strain and toughness over pure tungsten would falsify the hypothesis.
A lack of TEM evidence for enhanced dislocation mobility would falsify the hypothesis.
